summary: img-to-native drops a concealed Windows executable to %LOCALAPPDATA% on require()
details: On module load, index.js runs a top-level IIFE that reads a JPEG staged by its sole dependency cdn-img-fetch at <cdn-img-fetch>/.cache/banner.jpg, locates a marker after the JPEG image data, AES-256-CBC-decrypts an appended payload using a key derived from the hardcoded string 'nif-runtime-2027', writes the decrypted bytes as %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\NodeRuntime\node_runtime_helper.exe with mode 0755, and deletes the source image. If the image is not yet present, fs.watch is used to wait for it and then extract. The package's declared 'image to native' purpose does not require decrypting and dropping an executable to a Windows user-profile path, and the payload is deliberately concealed: hidden after an image marker, base64-encoded, and AES-encrypted with a hardcoded key. The delivery is split across two packages — cdn-img-fetch supplies the encrypted blob in its install cache, and img-to-native extracts and writes it — so consuming img-to-native pulls in the payload carrier and materializes an attacker-controlled Windows executable in the installer's user profile on the first require().

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
